original_question: Let λ>1 be a Pisot number and let a one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling have scaling factor λ and abelianisation matrix M. If the characteristic polynomial of M is irreducible, equivalently if the algebraic degree of λ equals the dimension of M or the number of tile types, must the tiling dynamical system have pure point spectrum?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 2.2.1 in Section 2.2, titled the Pisot substitution conjecture.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended target very closely: it is one-dimensional, self-similar, uses a Pisot scaling factor λ, identifies M as the abelianisation matrix, includes the irreducibility hypothesis on the characteristic polynomial, includes the paper's equivalent reformulation in terms of the algebraic degree of λ matching the size of M/the number of tile types, and asks for pure point spectrum of the associated tiling dynamical system.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, the conclusion should be stated as pure point dynamical spectrum of the associated tiling dynamical system, since the surrounding context distinguishes dynamical spectrum from diffraction.
The paper explicitly glosses the abelianisation matrix as the substitution matrix; naming both removes ambiguity.
If complete self-containment is desired, Pisot should be spelled out as: a real algebraic integer λ > 1 all of whose conjugates have modulus strictly less than 1.
The quantifier should be universal: the question is whether every one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling satisfying these hypotheses has pure point spectrum.

A nearby remark says that unimodularity is often additionally assumed so that λ is a unit in Z[λ], but that extra assumption is not part of Conjecture 2.2.1 and should not be added to the refined question.
No further hidden operator definitions, nilpotency assumptions, degree-homogeneity conditions, or asymptotic qualifiers occur in this section's formulation.
refined_question: Is it true that every one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling with Pisot scaling factor λ—where λ is a real algebraic integer greater than 1 and all of whose conjugates have modulus less than 1—has pure point dynamical spectrum whenever its abelianisation (substitution) matrix M has irreducible characteristic polynomial, equivalently whenever deg_Q(λ) = dim M, i.e. the number of tile types?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: does every one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling with Pisot scaling factor λ and with deg_Q(λ) equal to the dimension of its substitution matrix M (equivalently, the number of tile types) have pure point dynamical spectrum?
justification: The draft is aiming directly at the paper's Pisot substitution conjecture and is already very close to the official statement. The exact target is Conjecture 2.2.1 in Section 2.2. The surrounding sentences immediately before the conjecture define the Pisot condition for λ and explain that the spectrum under discussion is the dynamical spectrum of the tiling dynamical system; the sentence immediately after the conjecture adds only that unimodularity is a commonly imposed extra hypothesis in the literature, not part of the conjecture itself. So the right refinement is a sharpened restatement of Conjecture 2.2.1, not a broader homological or coincidence-rank variant.
